story.conflict: The narrator keeps finding small signs that strangers have been inside her apartment, while her sister insists she is imagining things and becomes defensive whenever questioned.
story.hook: I knew my sister was lying about my apartment when a stranger thanked me for 'renting it by the hour.'
story.premise: A woman lets her sister stay in her apartment for two weeks, then discovers her sister has been secretly charging coworkers to use it as a quiet daytime 'meeting suite' while the narrator is at work.
story.punchline: the only flaw was that she forgot to own the property.
story.script: My younger sister needed somewhere to stay for two weeks while her landlord repaired a burst pipe, so I gave her my spare key and told her to make herself comfortable. The first few days were normal. Then I came home and noticed my desk chair had been moved into the living room. She said she had been watching a movie and wanted somewhere more comfortable to sit. Fine. The next evening, there were two coffee cups in the sink even though she swore she had been alone all day. She laughed and said I was becoming weirdly territorial about mugs. Then I found a phone charger plugged in beside my sofa that belonged to neither of us. When I asked about it, she got irritated and told me I clearly didn't trust her. I started wondering if she was secretly bringing someone over, but every time I checked the building camera after work, I saw different people leaving. One man in a suit. Two women carrying laptops. Another guy wearing a headset. None of them stayed long. The next morning I worked from home without telling my sister. At eleven, someone knocked. A woman I had never seen before smiled, opened her laptop bag, and said she had booked the quiet room until noon. I just stared at her. My sister came running from the bedroom and tried to pull me aside, but the woman was already showing me the message thread. My sister had been advertising my apartment in her company group chat as a private meeting suite for coworkers whose homes were too noisy. Fifteen dollars an hour. Coffee included. She had even posted photos of my living room. I asked how much she had made. She quietly admitted it was almost six hundred dollars. Then she tried to explain that she was going to split it with me. I told her that was generous, considering she had contributed exactly zero apartments. She packed that afternoon, refunded the remaining bookings, and handed me every dollar she had collected. A week later one of her coworkers saw me in the lobby, waved cheerfully, and said, 'Your meeting room was great.' My sister still claims the business model was solid. I told her the only flaw was that she forgot to own the property.
story.twist: The sister is not throwing parties or hiding a boyfriend; she has listed the apartment in her office group chat as a paid private place for coworkers to take confidential calls and remote meetings.

youtube.description: I thought my sister was secretly inviting people over while I was at work. The truth was somehow even stranger: she had turned my apartment into a paid meeting room for her coworkers without telling me. #storytime #familydrama #funny #shorts
youtube.title: My Sister Secretly Rented Out My Apartment by the Hour
